We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy.

The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards https://www.gpbullhound.com/articles/allstars-awards-2026-winners-announced/, came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2026-20-uk-companies-rise-linkedin-news-uk-xoffc in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 https://scalingeurope.co.uk/ of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 https://lnkd.in/p/ehxWgJyc.

Learn more about us on our website https://www.tem.energy/.




🏅 THE ROLE:

We're hiring a Staff Full Stack Engineer to act as embedded technical leader for one of Buy-Side Growth's engineering squads.

Buy-Side is organised into four dedicated squads, each built around a single technical leader: Self-Driving Tendering, Price Everywhere, Broker Self-Serve, and Customer Autopilot, supported by a cross-squad Architect who owns the Buy Engine and tendering service. Two of those squads - Broker Self-Serve and Customer Autopilot - don't yet have a technical leader in place, which is the clearest gap in the team today. This role exists to close that gap: to be the person a squad looks to for architecture calls, technical direction, and the judgement to pick the right bets, without needing to be a people manager to do it.

The bigger picture: Buy-Side's vision is an engine that increasingly runs itself - agents handling tendering, pricing, and customer experience end to end, so the team can serve many more brokers and customers without headcount scaling in step. You'll be building directly toward that, on a team that already ships in dedicated, focused squads rather than one team context-switching across everything.

In your first 12 months, you might:

 - Step in as the embedded technical leader for a squad - most likely Broker Self-Serve or Customer Autopilot, both currently short a technical lead.

 - Take Customer Autopilot from pre-discovery to a shipped first version, setting its technical direction from scratch.

 - Extend the multi-broker tendering work that Self-Driving Tendering has already shipped, or push further into Price Everywhere, currently the team's biggest strategic bet.

 - Mentor the engineers around you, raising the technical bar for your squad through code review, architecture proposals, and the credibility of your own delivery.

 - Help design the agentic workflows that let Buy-Side handle dramatically more tenders and customers per person than it can today.




🚀 RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Build with impact: Architect and deliver end-to-end systems, from internal automation to broker- and customer-facing portals, ensuring they are scalable, fast, and user-friendly.

 - Lead the technical direction: Propose and own the technical direction for your squad, picking the right architectural bets and building the credibility to get others to act on your recommendations.

 - Own the platform: Improve and extend core platforms and tooling, making it easier for your squad and others to build, test, and ship quality software.

 - Drive innovation: Rapidly prototype and iterate on new workflows and product ideas that expand our offering and improve the broker and customer journey.

 - Raise the bar: Mentor other engineers and teach your domain through code reviews and hands-on collaboration, without needing a formal management line to do it.




🎯 REQUIREMENTS:

Must-Haves:

 - Strong technical leadership: a track record of setting technical direction for a team or project, and getting others to commit to it through the credibility of your work, not through a management title.

 - Track record in fast-paced environments: experience as a Senior or Staff Engineer in a high-growth startup or scale-up, with a strong bias toward shipping.

 - System design at scale: proven ability to design and build complex systems that power both back-end automation and front-end experiences.

 - Modern tech expertise: it's preferred that someone has deep experience with Python (FastAPI) and modern JavaScript/TypeScript frameworks such as React, however we're open to people who demonstrate the ability to be tech agnostic. 

 - Product-minded: experience participating and leading customer discovery calls in translating user needs into feature ideations, following the end-to-end lifecycle of a product offering. 

 - Can deal with ambiguity: comfortable navigating changing priorities and incomplete information to make strong technical decisions, particularly useful for a squad like Customer Autopilot that's still pre-discovery.

Desirable:

 - Agentic or agent-building experience: exposure to designing multi-agent workflows or systems, which is central to Buy-Side's long-term direction.

 - Exposure to the energy sector or other regulated industries.

 - Experience building internal tools or platforms for brokers, sales teams, or support agents.

 - Familiarity with real-time data processing systems.




✨ BENEFITS & PERKS:

 - Competitive salary - our current band for this role is £104,000 or equivalent in local currency.
   
   - We pay against a clear benchmark for your role and level. No fixed once- or twice-a-year cycle - pay moves when the evidence for it does.

 - Stock Options - everyone on the team has ownership in our mission.

 - 25 days holiday + public holidays - Swap public holidays for ones that matter most to you. Plus, get an extra day off for your birthday 🎉.

 - Remote & flexible working - We’re fully remote with clear core hours, and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

 - Home working & wellbeing budgets:
   
   - Up to £1,200 / €1,200 annually to upgrade your remote setup (co-working passes, equipment, etc.).
   
   - Up to £150 / €150 monthly on anything that supports your wellbeing - from therapy to gym memberships to meditation apps.




🗣️ INTERVIEW PROCESS:

Our processes normally take around 2-3 weeks from first call to offer - please let us know about any adjustments to timelines that may be required.

 1. First call with our Talent Team (30 Mins). This is to understand your experience, motivations, and discuss the role in more detail.

 2. Behaviour Interview with our Engineering Managers (60 Mins). This is your chance to really understand the role, the expectations, and ensure alignment on ways of working.

 3. Technical Interview with the Team (75 Mins). You’ll meet with potential peers in this session and will discuss technical topics and experiences.

 4. Bar Raiser Interview with Stakeholders (45 Mins). The final session will be with two cross-functional stakeholders, and will explore how your values align with ours, and is designed to be a genuine two-way conversation, your chance to understand what it’s really like to work at tem.



We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

🏅 The Role:

Rosso is tem's core IP, the transaction infrastructure that prices electricity for thousands of businesses, balances portfolios in real time, and sits on the critical path for every deal tem closes. Machine learning is at the heart of Rosso, combining forecasting, optimisation and classical ML to process billions of data points and drive thousands of automated decisions a day. Every inference shapes the prices our customers see, so you can immediately see the impact of your work.

We have proved the concept with MVPs and POCs to grow to 2% of the UK market. Now we want to take it to the next level and build towards a state of the art solution, to fuel our expansion in the UK and take Rosso international.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead pricing ML within Rosso, building a platform that proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time. Your primary focus will be the pricing engine, which sets the fees added to every quote tem serves, carefully balancing growth and margin. You will also contribute to the systems which manage both short and long-term imbalance decisions to determine how tem deals with its exposure across its portfolio.



This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role. You own the technical direction of pricing by building it: most of your week is writing and shipping production code. It is not a people leadership role, and not an architecture role where others do the implementing.

The right person is energised by the greenfield environment: comfortable taking on ambiguity and able to make progress before the path is fully defined. They have built pricing, trading or optimisation systems that worked, ideally in energy or another market-driven domain, and have learned from the times they haven't. They'll bring that hard-won judgment to a system where the foundations are still being laid, and where early decisions compound. Success will be turning our current reactive system into a pricing engine which proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time.



🚀 Responsibilities:

 - Own the technical direction for pricing ML: Define what to build and how within the pricing engine, setting the strategy and roadmap for pricing machine learning as a core piece of tem's IP.

 - Build ML systems for price optimisation: Design and implement models that dynamically set prices, balancing the trade-off between signing probability, portfolio balance and margin maximisation.

 - Solve imbalance problems: Develop probabilistic models to optimise risk management and short-term balancing decisions in a highly dynamic environment.

 - Bridge modelling and production: Own the modelling and data layer while working closely with software engineers and MLOps to ensure models are architected for production, contributing to system design decisions that affect performance and reliability.

 - Communicate pricing decisions clearly: Articulate model behaviour, assumptions, and trade-offs to other technical stakeholders so that pricing decisions are understood across the teams that depend on them.



🎯 Requirements:

Must-haves:

 - Deep experience building ML systems for pricing, revenue optimisation, or decision-making under uncertainty, with a track record of models that went from concept to production and delivered measurable commercial impact.

 - A quantitative background in a domain where prices, forecasts and risk interact: energy markets, power trading, batteries and flexibility, market making, or similar. Energy is strongly preferred and where our strongest fits have come from.

 - Strong foundation in stochastic optimisation and probabilistic modelling, with the judgement to formulate ambiguous business problems as the right mathematical approach rather than reaching for familiar tools.

 - Proven first-principles reasoning: you choose between stochastic programming, classical ML, reinforcement learning, or a simple heuristic based on the problem, not the technique you know best.

 - The engineering craft to match your modelling depth: production-grade Python, a high bar for code quality and system design, and the ability to work alongside software engineers as a technical peer across the full ML lifecycle.

 - Breadth across the full lifecycle: you carry the modelling and quant work and the productionising (deploying, monitoring, reasoning about the software systems around your models), and you would rather ship the whole thing to a good standard and iterate than perfect one component. You reason at the level of the outcome, the portfolio and its levers, not a single model.

Bonus points:

 - Experience with reinforcement learning or causal inference in applied, commercial settings.

 - PhD or equivalent research depth in a quantitative discipline (statistics, applied mathematics, physics, operations research, or similar).

 - Ability to reason about the trade-offs between optimisation solvers (Gurobi etc) and gradient-based ML methods (PyTorch etc), and the judgement to know when to reach for each.

 - Experience working with high data throughput systems in production.

✨ Benefits & Perks:

 - Stock Options: everyone on the team has ownership in our mission.

🏅 The Role:

We're hiring a Staff Machine Learning Engineer (L4) for Pricing in Rosso.

Rosso is tem's core IP. It forecasts prices and volumes, holds a live view of our portfolio, and sets the fees on every quote. You'll join the pricing ML team and own key components of our dynamic pricing system. The direction is set. Within your components, choosing the bets and proving whether they worked is yours. This is a hands-on role. Most of your week will be writing and shipping production code, and you'll stay accountable for what that code does once it's live.

You will:

 - Own key components of our dynamic pricing system end to end, from design through to running them in production.

 - Choose the bets within those components most likely to reduce sales adjustment, and show whether they worked.

 - Make your components observable, guarded and replayable, so a wrong price is caught before a customer sees it.

 - Unblock your own delivery across engineering, platform and commercial teams.

You will report into the ML Leader for Rosso.



🚀 Responsibilities:

 - Own key components of dynamic pricing
   
   - Take ownership of one or more core components, such as the models that learn from won and lost deals, the experimentation and measurement layer, or the live guardrails that keep price changes safe.
   
   - Within your components, choose between competing bets based on which is most likely to move the metric, and stop the ones that don't.
   
   - Design experiments and holdouts that work with low-volume, high-value deals, where a textbook A/B test often isn't possible.
   
   Run it live, safely
   
   - Build the monitoring, alerting, guardrails and staged release your components need. That includes detecting drift, catching runaway feedback loops and holding unexpected price moves for review.
   
   - Make any pricing decision your components produce reproducible after the fact, for debugging and for regulators.
   
   - Work with the Price Quoting squad and ML Platform so models are built for production from the start, not handed over at the end.
   
   Close the loop with the business
   
   - Find out why sales teams adjust prices, and turn those reasons into model inputs or new bets.
   
   - Explain model behaviour and trade-offs to engineers, product and commercial colleagues clearly enough that they can act on it.
   
   - Redesign the team's recurring pricing workflows with AI built in, such as feedback triage, daily price review and experiment write-ups. Decide which steps stay human.🎯 



🎯 Requirements:

Must-haves:

 - You build. Most of your current role is writing and shipping production code, and you want to keep it that way. This is not a people leadership role or an architecture role where others implement.

 - You have owned a live ML system that made automated decisions with money attached, for example in algorithmic trading, dynamic pricing, marketplaces, ad bidding, credit or betting. You have dealt with its failures in production, such as feedback loops, silent drift, bad outputs reaching customers and rollbacks, and changed how you build because of them.

 - Strong probabilistic modelling and decision-making under uncertainty, such as pricing, conversion or elasticity modelling, and experimentation. You formulate the problem from first principles and pick the simplest approach that works.

 - You've run ML as production services on modern cloud infrastructure: containerised models behind APIs, event-driven microservices, infrastructure as code and CI/CD on AWS or similar. Your model changes go through the same pipeline, tests and rollback as any other code, so shipping one on a Thursday afternoon is routine.

 - Production-grade Python, and a habit of designing for observability, testing and replay. You work as a peer with software engineers.

 - A track record of moving a commercial metric, working alongside product managers and commercial stakeholders to get there.

 - You use AI tooling as a day-to-day multiplier on your own work, and you know where it fails.

Energy experience is not required. We will teach you the market. What we can't teach quickly is the judgement that comes from running a live pricing or trading system.

 - Experience in energy, commodities or other markets where prices, forecasts and risk interact.

 - Contextual bandits, causal inference or Bayesian methods used in production.

 - Stochastic optimisation or operations research.

 - A PhD in a field such as maths, physics, computer science or operations research.

 - Stock Options: everyone on the team has ownership in our mission.

   - Up to £1,200 / €1,200 annually to upgrade your remote setup (co-working passes, equipment, etc.).
   
   - Up to £150 / €150 monthly on anything that supports your wellbeing, from therapy to gym memberships to meditation apps.

 1. First call with our Talent Team (30 mins). This is to understand your experience, motivations, and discuss the role in more detail.

 2. Behavioural interview with our Rosso GM, hiring manager for this role (30 mins). This is your chance to really understand the role, the expectations, and ensure alignment on ways of working.

 3. Technical interview with the Team (90 mins). You'll meet with potential peers in this session and work through a live technical exercise.

 4. Bar Raiser interview with Stakeholders (45 mins). The final session will be with two cross-functional stakeholders.
